title: Advances in PPARs Molecular Dynamics and Glitazones as a Repurposing Therapeutic Strategy through Mitochondrial Redox Dynamics against Neurodegeneration.
authors: Durai, Priya; Beeraka, Narasimha M; Ramachandrappa, Hemanth Vikram Poola; Krishnan, Prakash; Gudur, Pranesh; Raghavendra, Nulgumnalli Manjunathaiah; Ravanappa, Prashantha Kumar Bommenahally
one_liner_zh: 综述PPAR核受体配体互作与线粒体氧化还原在神经退行性疾病中的治疗潜力，涉及核受体-配体结合但非TF-DNA互作建模，方法上仅提及分子动力学而无AI/物理模拟核心研究。
abstract: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) activity has significant implications for the development of novel therapeutic modalities against neurodegenerative diseases. Although PPAR-alpha, PPAR-beta/delta, and PPAR-gamma nuclear receptor expressions are significantly reported in the brain, their implications in brain physiology and other neurodegenerative diseases still require extensive studies. PPAR signaling can modulate various cell signaling mechanisms involved in the cells contributing to on- and off-target actions selectively to promote therapeutic effects as well as the adverse effects of PPAR ligands. Both natural and synthetic ligands for the PPARalpha, PPARgamma, and PPARbeta/delta have been reported. PPARalpha (WY 14.643) and PPARgamma agonists can confer neuroprotection by modulating mitochondrial dynamics through the redox system. The pharmacological effect of these agonists may deliver effective clinical responses by protecting vulnerable neurons from Abeta toxicity in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients. Therefore, the current review delineated the ligands' interaction with 3D-PPARs to modulate neuroprotection, and also deciphered the efficacy of numerous drugs, viz. Abeta aggregation inhibitors, vaccines, and gamma-secretase inhibitors against AD; this review elucidated the role of PPAR and their receptor isoforms in neural systems, and neurodegeneration in human beings. Further, we have substantially discussed the efficacy of PPREs as potent transcription factors in the brain, and the role of PPAR agonists in neurotransmission, PPAR gamma coactivator-1alpha (PGC-1alpha) and mitochondrial dynamics in neuroprotection during AD conditions. This review concludes with the statement that the development of novel PPARs agonists may benefit patients with neurodegeneration, mainly AD patients, which may help mitigate the pathophysiology of dementia, subsequently improving overall the patient's quality of life.
abstract_zh: 过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARs）活性对开发针对神经退行性疾病的新型治疗模式具有重要意义。尽管PPAR-alpha、PPAR-beta/delta和PPAR-gamma核受体在大脑中的表达已被显著报道，但它们在大脑生理及其他神经退行性疾病中的作用仍需广泛研究。PPAR信号传导可调节参与细胞的各种细胞信号机制，选择性地作用于靶标和非靶标效应，以促进PPAR配体的治疗效果及不良效应。已报道有PPARalpha、PPARgamma和PPARbeta/delta的天然及合成配体。PPARalpha（WY 14.643）和PPARgamma激动剂可通过氧化还原系统调节线粒体动力学来赋予神经保护作用。这些激动剂的药理效应可能通过保护阿尔茨海默病（AD）患者中易受损神经元免受Abeta毒性影响，从而提供有效的临床反应。因此，本综述详细阐述了配体与三维PPARs的相互作用以调节神经保护，并解析了多种药物（如Abeta聚集抑制剂、疫苗和γ-分泌酶抑制剂）对抗AD的疗效；本综述阐明了PPAR及其受体亚型在人类神经系统和神经退行性变中的作用。此外，我们充分讨论了PPREs作为大脑中强效转录因子的功效，以及PPAR激动剂在神经传递中的作用、PPARγ共激活因子-1alpha（PGC-1alpha）和线粒体动力学在AD条件下神经保护中的角色。本综述总结指出，开发新型PPARs激动剂可能有益于神经退行性疾病患者，尤其是AD患者，这可能有助于缓解痴呆的病理生理过程，进而改善患者的整体生活质量。
